content:
Samir: Heads-up — Concorda wants to POC a migration off RivalAPI to Redwood. Main asks: prove prompt/response parity, clarify pricing delta (hosted vs reserved vs private), and complete their security questionnaire. Can we sketch a tight POC + runbook?
Jasmin: +1. Proposed scope: 2-week POC. Week 0: network + questionnaire. Week 1: adapter + smoke tests. Week 2: evaluation (500 prompts) + pricing decision.
Oliver: For pricing we can offer: 1) Hosted PAYG credits for the POC, 2) 30% trial discount on a 6mo reserved commit, 3) Private deployment quote (flat infra + support). I can share numbers after we estimate token delta.
Marta: Security checklist early: SOC2 cert, DPA + SCCs, KMS bring-your-own-key, IP allowlist, data retention policy, and Azure VPC peering requirements. ETA to fill their questionnaire: 48–72 hrs once we have contact.
Ravi: Compatibility notes: RivalAPI expects header X-Rival-Model and returns a slightly different function-calling JSON shape. We can do a lightweight adapter that rewrites headers and normalizes function outputs. Important: token accounting may differ (Rival uses gpt2 tokenization assumptions). Expect ±3–8% token divergence in some prompts.
Lina: For prompt parity, we should do an A/B harness: send same prompt to Rival and Redwood, capture: (1) semantic similarity (embedding cosine), (2) structural match (function call vs text), (3) token delta. Add a small metric dashboard (accuracy, avg latency, median tokens).
Samir: Blockers from Concorda: they require private VPC for any PII, and legal needs DPA & SCCs signed before prod. Also they asked about our rollback policy if outputs differ in prod.
Marta: We have a standard rollback and can pin model version + automatic fallback to a smaller-capacity variant. For private VPC: we support Azure peering and can integrate with their KMS (Azure Key Vault) or allow HSM via dedicated.
deploy-bot: VPC image for private POC is available in staging. To proceed we need: customer Azure subscription ID, list of CIDR blocks, and expected QPS.
Jasmin: I'll own the POC runbook. Action items: 1) Samir to get Concorda SRE contact & prompt corpus (500 examples). 2) Oliver to send preliminary pricing ranges. 3) Marta to start questionnaire. 4) Ravi & Lina to prepare adapter + evaluation harness. Timeline: kickoff this week, initial smoke in 3 business days.
Oliver: I'll email Concorda pricing options EOD and propose the 2-week POC scope.
Ravi: Quick adapter sketch (for reference):
```
rewrite_request(req) {
  req.headers['X-Redwood-Model'] = mapModel(req.headers['X-Rival-Model'])
  // preserve original prompt, add metadata: origin=Rival-migration
}
```
Also add token-count check before/after response to compute delta.
Lina: Edge case tests: function-calling ordering, streaming chunk boundaries, and stop-sequence behavior. We'll include 20 function-call prompts in the eval set.
Samir: Concorda (Alex) — can you drop the SRE contact + sample prompts here? Also confirm whether PII will be included.
Alex (Concorda): Thanks — will share SRE contact (marie@sconcorda) and a redacted prompt corpus by EOD. PII: only hashed IDs for the POC. We prefer private VPC but can start hosted if easier.
Marta: Noted. If only hashed IDs, hosted with a strict retention policy might be ok for POC. For production they'll require Private.
Jasmin: I'll draft the runbook and post here in the morning. Quick Q: who owns the adapter infra during POC — Engineering or Solutions?
Ravi: Eng will spin the adapter in staging, but Solutions can own orchestration & evaluation scripts. After POC handoff we can recommend either Managed Dedicated or Private depending on results.
Samir: Perfect. Thanks all — I'll coordinate with Concorda and update this thread with contacts and the prompt set. :thumbsup:
